title: Lean 4 formalization of Lavi's proof of Foregger's conjecture
description:
A sorry-free Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Sections 2–7 of Y. Lavi, Foregger's Conjecture on Minimum Permanents of Nearly Decomposable Doubly Stochastic Matrices (preprint, 2026), ending with the paper's Theorem 1.1. foregger_conjecture (also lavi_theorem_1_1_unconditional) states that for n ≥ 2, every doubly stochastic n × n matrix A with nearly decomposable support has per A ≥ 2^(1−n), with equality exactly when A is obtained from (1/2)(I + P), P an n-cycle permutation matrix, by independent row and column permutations. lavi_theorem_1_1_moreover_unconditional states that on every nearly decomposable face whose support is not a cycle support, the minimum of the permanent is attained and exceeds 2^(1−n).

Gurvits's inequality. The proof uses Gurvits's degree-sensitive capacity inequality for permanents (L. Gurvits, Electron. J. Combin. 15 (2008), Theorem 2.4 and Corollary 2.7(a); M. Laurent and A. Schrijver, Amer. Math. Monthly 117 (2010), Corollary 1a). Version 1.2.0 assumed it as an explicit hypothesis; since version 1.3.0 it is proved (gurvitsCapacityInequality), building on the Lean formalization of Gurvits's stable-polynomial argument in the RealRooted library by Per Alexandersson and contributors (https://github.com/PerAlexandersson/RealRooted, commit d667074, Apache-2.0). The degree-sensitive step adapts RealRooted's proof, with the degree in the eliminated variable in place of the total degree.

Checks. The main theorems depend only on Lean's standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), and the repository contains no sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide. The dependency closure of the final theorems, including Mathlib and RealRooted, was re-checked by Lean's kernel in a fresh environment (leanchecker --fresh) and by the independent type checkers nanoda, lean4lean and con-leche. CI runs an axiom allowlist and nanoda on every push.

Review status. The Lean statements were compared with the paper and found faithful for n ≥ 2. They have not yet been reviewed by a second person.

The formalization also records simplifications of several arguments, listed in the README (for example Lemma 3.1 without Lagrange multipliers or Sinkhorn scaling, the removability rule (4.3) by a strict-Hall computation, the secant bounds (5.10) by Bernoulli's inequality, and an equality argument that avoids the edge count).

Version 1.3.1 revises the documentation only; the Lean code is unchanged from version 1.3.0.
